summary: ansible-core 2.12 module changes: cron requires name and drops reboot (use special_time: reboot), hostname's before result is an empty string instead of placeholders on FreeBSD, OpenRC and Solaris, and pip uses the pip module of the module's Python interpreter.
questions: cron fails asking for name, why?
How do I create an @reboot cron job now?
Why does pip install into a different Python than before?
hostname before is now empty on FreeBSD, is that expected?

answer_card.title: cron, hostname and pip changes in 2.12
answer_card.answer_md:
- `cron`: **`name` is required**; `reboot: yes` removed, use:

```yaml
- cron:
    name: run at boot
    special_time: reboot
    job: /usr/local/bin/startup.sh
```

- `hostname`: `before` is `""` instead of `temporarystub` (FreeBSD) or `UNKNOWN` (OpenRC/Solaris) when no permanent hostname file exists.
- `pip`: uses the pip module of the interpreter running the module, unless `executable` or `virtualenv` is set.
